newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes Chemical to spin off business.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes Chemical to spin off business.

text.p: Great Lakes Chemical Corp said Thursday its board of directors approved a plan to spin off its Octel petroleum additives business to shareholders.

The independent company created by the spinoff will consist of Octel Associates, which makes tetraethyl lead antiknock compounds and petroleum additives, and Octel America, which develops and markets peformance-enhancing fuel additives.

Great Lakes said reached agreement with Chevron Chemical Co, a unit of Chevron Corp, for Octel to acquire a 10.65 percent interest in it held by Chevron. This transaction is expected to be completed by the end of September.
Prior to the spinoff, Octel will raise about $450 million through public and private borrowings and use a portion of the proceeds to repay a loan for the Chevron transaction.

The remainder of the proceeds and available cash from Octel, less taxes and transaction costs, will be distributed to Great Lakes in a special distribution of roughly $300 million before the spin-off is completed, the company said.

Great Lakes said the transaction will be a tax-free distribution to shareholders and is expected to be completed in about nine months. The transaction is subject to receipt of a favorable ruling from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, the acquisition of all existing minority interests in Octel, and final approval by the Great Lakes board.

"Separating Great Lakes into two independently owned and operated companies will enable each company to better focus on its markets and pursue its individual strategies more effectively," Robert McDonald, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
McDonald added that the spinoff will allow each company to align its compensation and incentive programs more directly with the performance of its businesses.

"The management team already in place at Octel is uniquely qualified to maximize the cash flow and earnings from the lead antiknock business and transform Octel into a broad-based petrolum additives company," McDonald said.
Dennis Kerrison, 52, currently the managing director of Octel, will continue to head that business.
